set.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. Aspen In Chains is the tallest climb on this rock.
set.descent_text: The two-bolt anchor carries rap rings; descend by rappelling from them.

review.notes: Route and area pages: access from campsite 9 and the descent to the base; anchor with rap rings.

set.approach: Drive up the Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) road past Lincoln Lake, the long lake on the left before Summit Lake. The slabs are the obvious rock features rising right beside the road, with small pullouts on the drop-off side at and after the corner where the road crosses above the last cliff. Balisong follows the painted bolts between Gettysburg Address and Pika, and can finish on either anchor.

review.notes: Area page: roadside pullouts; route page: painted bolts between Gettysburg Address and Pika. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the middle of three pullouts across the highway from the Halidome (the Al Cap pullout), cross the road and go up a short rise to a large scree field. Climb the scree toward its narrowing top; cairns may mark the way. Near the top the terrain funnels you to a gap in the cliff band under the main wall, where a steep earthen path climbs left along the base of the Halidome. When it levels out you pass the start of Pandemonium on the right, an open-book dihedral; soon after you reach The Zephyr, whose first pitch has a right-facing gash near its top.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route; the anchors are fitted for quick rappels, and the longer pitches need knots in the rope ends. A walk-off exists from the top by going climber's right to the gully and down, or off the catwalk ledge above the third pitch.

review.notes: Single route page gives the approach and the descent (rappel the route, walk-off alternative).

set.approach: Take County Road 805 to the gate and park near it without blocking the road. Walk down the road past a cabin, then at the next creek sign bear left and go uphill to a talus field and the cliff; aim for the top of the mine tailings field. The crag faces north on Northstar Mountain. Angry Pika is the left of the two bolted routes in the middle of the crag.

review.notes: Area page: road, gate and talus approach; route page: position on the crag. No descent stated.

set.approach: Although the cliffs lie within Arapaho National Forest, the simplest access crosses private property: with permission, walk south from the trailhead a little way inside the Latigo Ranch gate. The other way is to walk due east from the forest service road through the trees. Rose's Cantina starts downhill, on the climber's left, of Bless You.

review.notes: Area page: the two approaches; route page: position beside Bless You. No descent stated.

set.approach: Quartzite pillar The Citadel stands north of Rolling Stones Wall and Tradistan Tower, so the approach follows theirs. From the Pine River trailhead at the end of the road around Vallecito Lake, hike the Pine River trail until the Indian Creek drainage appears on the left, staying on the trail until then because it crosses private land by easement. Stay on the west side of the creek and make an ascending traverse to the right on faint elk trails and cairns to the base of Tradistan Tower; a huge cave about halfway up its wall is a landmark. Traverse left along the base around the toe of Tradistan, then go up left on scrambling and angle back right along ledges to the Rolling Stones Wall. Audrey starts from the ledge reached by climbing the first two pitches of Texas Wheelchair, then crossing a good ledge to the right to reach the base of a bolted dihedral.

review.notes: Route page: start via Texas Wheelchair; area pages: the approach chain to the Citadel. No descent stated.

Stay on the west side of the creek and make an ascending traverse to the right on faint elk trails and cairns to the base of Tradistan Tower; a huge cave about halfway up its wall is a landmark. set.approach: Furiosa begins a short way right of The Nose, with an easy two-bolt slab pitch reaching a bolted anchor on a grubby ledge, above which the main pitch uses cracks and then a pocketed face up and left.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors; a long enough rope reaches the ground in a single rappel.

review.notes: Route page only. No crag approach is stated on any Thunderdome Buttress page.

set.approach: Juice starts from the Master Blaster anchor: follow the ramp that angles left to the higher anchor on the right, atop the formation known as the Anvil. Reach the Master Blaster anchor by climbing Master Blaster, or by climbing Bartertown to its second ledge.
set.descent_text: Descend Road Warrior by rappel to the Master Blaster anchor, then rappel again to the ground.

review.notes: Own page: start from the Master Blaster anchor and the two-stage rappel. No crag approach is stated on any Thunderdome Buttress page.

set.approach: Master Blaster starts on Bartertown. Climb Bartertown to its second ledge, where a two-bolt anchor serves this route, and begin from there; the first bolt is a little above the ledge.

review.notes: Route page only. No crag approach and no descent is stated on this route page.

set.approach: To reach the start, climb Master Blaster, or climb Bartertown to its second anchor up and to the right on the big ledge and then rappel the Road Warrior bolts down to the Master Blaster anchor. Road Warrior climbs the bolted line to the right of that anchor to the same anchor as Juice.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route back to the Master Blaster anchor, then make one more rappel to the ground. Do not go to the Furiosa anchor, which lies off to the side.

review.notes: Own page: start via Master Blaster anchor and the two-stage rappel. No crag approach is stated on any Thunderdome Buttress page.

set.approach: The Nose forms the middle of Thunderdome Buttress, and the route starts just above the approach trail. It climbs five bolts to a big ledge with a two-bolt anchor, which is the base for the overhanging corner routes above.

review.notes: Route page only; no crag approach is stated on any Thunderdome Buttress page.

set.approach: War Boys starts from the ledge anchor at the top of Furiosa's approach pitch: climb that pitch and belay there. The route is the left-facing overhanging rhyolite corner just right of Furiosa.

review.notes: Own page: start from Furiosa's approach pitch and the corner just right of Furiosa. No crag approach is stated on any Thunderdome Buttress page; no descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the town park in Telluride and follow Bear Creek upstream to the boulder named for it, below the main waterfall. From there, follow the Wasatch trail above the main falls to a point short of the bridge, wade over to the east side of the drainage, and traverse the obvious trail under the red clay cliffs toward the walls. Smokey the Bear lies beyond the vertical break in the wall, just right of Wildfire, which is easy to spot by its second-pitch roof and corner.

review.notes: Area page: trail options; route page: position right of Wildfire.
